why_it_matters: It is the shortcut behind half of trigonometry: know sin, and cos comes free. Calculators, game engines and rotating images all lean on it.

concepts.text: sin = opposite ÷ hypotenuse and cos = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse (the definitions)
In a right triangle a² + b² = c² (the Pythagorean theorem)
Squaring both ratios and adding them gives (opp² + adj²) ÷ hyp² = hyp² ÷ hyp² = 1, so sin² + cos² = 1

misconception: sin x + cos x = 1, even though 3/5 + 4/5 comes out 1.4 when I check it
root_prerequisite: The Pythagorean theorem and the definitions of sine and cosine

boss.name: Baroness Plus-Plus-One
boss.backstory: An owl in a monocle who carries a sign reading 'SIN + COS = 1' and insists that 3/5 + 4/5 is one.

taunt: Three fifths plus four fifths is one. I have checked. Twice. Badly.
The squares are decorative. I have removed them.
heal: Splendid. Plain addition makes one. I shall have it engraved.
Quite right. The squares were never invited.
hit: This is most irregular. The squares appear to have returned.
I did not authorize a hypotenuse in the denominator.
lines.reformed: I have restored the squares. Three fifths plus four fifths is, in fact, not one. I would like to join you.

cliffhanger: I heard the same trick makes 1 + tan² turn into something with sec. Is that just dividing again? That can't be right… right?

quiz.question: In a 3-4-5 right triangle, what are sin and cos of the angle opposite the side 3?
A right triangle has legs 3 and 4. What is the hypotenuse?
What is sin 30° + cos 30°, and what is sin² 30° + cos² 30°? (sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° ≈ 0.87)
